(Contact+Manager.swift:1642, OccultaApp.swift:889-891). A re-opened, already-consumed forward-secret .occ from the transport history, or a crafted bundle built from a public key or a card file, therefore tells a coercer whether its sender is a current hidden contact. The code already uses 'reject as an unrecognised sender' to hide a known sender in one place (Contact+Manager.swift:2018-2019).

hardening: Identity challenge from a hidden contact at a duress depth: approvePending signs and encrypts a response to the hidden challenger through encryptBundle, which has no visibility guard and pops the hidden contact's prekey (IdentityChallenge+Coordinator.swift:263-304, Contact+Manager.swift:1069, :1129-1131). Inbound processing time scales with total contacts and issued cards across all depths (identifyOwner per-contact key decrypt with per-call local key derivation, Contact+Manager.swift:1616-1625; legacy trial decrypt :1000-1020; redeemCard ECDH per issued card per slot, ContactManager+Cards.swift:622-640). The slot AEAD authenticates only `blind` (Crypto+Manager+GroupDecrypt.swift:161) and the pre-consumption digest covers only `bundle.ciphertext` (:167). The outer `secrecy.ephemeralPublicKey` and `secrecy.prekeyID` come from cleartext wire bytes (WireHandle.swift:52-54, :67; OccultaBundle.swift:902) and are authenticated only as the outer AAD in openGroupCiphertext (:214-217, called at Contact+Manager.swift:2008), after the defer at :145-148 has consumed the key and SenderPrekeys has saved and checkpointed the record (Contact+Manager+Prekeys.swift:251-258, :109-116). local_checks.invariant: On a slot that opens again (long-term or last-resort), PrekeyBookkeeper.accept must refuse a replayed batch, even after its ID has left the 8-entry window. It must do this whatever dates the contact's clock gave batches accepted since then, which the comment at PrekeyBookkeeper.swift:142 claims for a clock-back sender.
local_checks.result: Violated at the boundary. The date gate is strict `generatedAt < newest` (PrekeyBookkeeper.swift:134), and `latestInboundGeneratedAt` is the maximum ever accepted (:144). Batches accepted on one-time slots need only a new ID (:133, :135-138), so a contact whose clock is behind the maximum can push the max-dated batch's ID out of the window, and the window does not raise `newest`. A replay of that batch on a reopenable slot then has generatedAt == newest. It passes the gate, its stale keys are appended (:147), and inboundLastResort is replaced (:152). Existing replay tests cover only replays aged out by batches with later dates (PrekeyBookkeeperTests.swift:784). The plist codec keeps full Date precision, so no rounding changes this. Candidate prekey-accept-reopenable-slot-replay-of-newest-dated-batch.

local_checks.invariant: acceptInboundBatch classifies a slot as reopenable exactly when its key survives the open: long-term, last-resort and card-agreement-key slots are reopenable; one-time slots are not.

hardening: openGroup throws GroupDecryptError.missingGroupID at Contact+Manager.swift:2081, after `save(prekeys, for: sender)` at :2074. A bundle rejected for having no groupID has already persisted its accepted batch, updateMaxVersion, applyCardOpening and any batch replenish generated. This contradicts the Bug 159 comment at :2069-2072. Only the genuine sender, or a rewriter of a digest-less body (the known Bug 165 residual), can produce such a body, so no boundary is crossed. Move the guard above step 6.

Legacy keychain one-time prekeys are classed `.oneTime`, so acceptInboundBatch treats their slot as single-use (Contact+Manager+Prekeys.swift:128). Their deletion, PrekeySecretsManager.consume (PrekeySecretsManager.swift:147-163), is best-effort, and a failed SecItemDelete leaves a slot that reopens without the reopenable-slot date gate. This needs a keychain failure and lasts at most until legacy keys retire (30 days).

openGroup strips shard content on long-term, last-resort and card slots (Contact+Manager.swift:2090), but returns an identity challenge from those reopenable slots on every redelivery. Whether IdentityChallenge.Coordinator.handleAuthenticatedChallenge deduplicates a replayed request or response belongs to the IdentityChallenge peer unit and was not assessed here.

PrekeySecretsManager.retrieveKey prints 'Could not retrieve private key to decrypt message.' with debugPrint outside `#if DEBUG` (PrekeySecretsManager.swift:278), so Release builds write it to stdout on every keychain miss, including each trial-decryption miss. Elsewhere in these files such logging is DEBUG-only. Stdout is not normally persisted on iOS, but it is easy to gate.

The GroupEnvelope TLV is JSON-decoded in full (OccultaBundle.swift:906) before the 32-slot cap (Crypto+Manager+GroupDecrypt.swift:136-138; ContactManager+Cards.swift:619), so decode memory scales with the file. This is the known unbounded inbound read (SecurityReview2026-07-24 finding #11, LOW), not a new item. A slot cap in the TLV parse would bound it.

SignedAttributeCodec.encode (Vault+Model.swift:415, 420) guards only negative dates (max(0, …)); a value >= 2^64 still traps. It is reachable only if handleHandback skips its own verify (retrieveIdentity failing) and acceptReturnedShard stores the attribute. The fix for OccultaFormats/SignedAttribute.signingPayload:out-of-range-date-to-UInt64-trap at decode time closes it too.

CardMeeting.transcript frames elements with UInt16(clamping:) (CardMeeting.swift:34), so elements longer than 65,535 bytes lose unambiguous framing. Callers must bound identity-key, nonce and ML-KEM ciphertext lengths before calling it; that was not checked here (in-person exchange peer unit).

local_checks.result: deriveSymmetricKey computes SecKeyCopyKeyExchangeResult(privateKey, .ecdhKeyExchangeCofactorX963SHA256, G) (ShareStagingKeyManager.swift:141-152). For P-256 (cofactor 1) ECDH of private scalar d with the generator G is d*G, the key's own public point Q, so rawSecret = X9.63-SHA256(x(Q)). The HKDF salt is Q itself (:154-164) and info is a constant (:37). Every input is a function of the public key; the Enclave adds no secrecy.
